verdict: Apple set a December-quarter record with revenue up 4% to $124.3B — Services hit an all-time high of $26.3B and Mac and iPad both grew double digits — keeping $36.3B as profit even though iPhone sales dipped slightly.

segments.name: iPhone
segments.note: Apple's flagship smartphone — the iPhone 16 family; sales dipped 1% YoY.

segments.name: Mac
segments.note: Mac computers — new M4-powered MacBook Pro, iMac and Mac mini models lifted sales 16%.

segments.name: iPad
segments.note: iPad tablets — new iPad Air and mini models lifted sales 15%.

segments.name: Wearables, Home and Accessories
segments.note: Apple Watch, AirPods, HomePod, Apple TV and accessories; down 2% YoY.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, Apple Pay, Apple TV+ and licensing — an all-time high, up 14% YoY.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Spending to design future products and technologies.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Sales, marketing and day-to-day running costs.

follow100Note: iPhone is $55.62 of every $100 Apple takes in; Services adds another $21.19. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Segments are net sales by product category, as Apple reports them.

takeaways.title: Services set another record
takeaways.text: Services revenue reached an all-time high of $26.3B, up 14% — more than a fifth of everything Apple sells, at much higher margins than hardware.

takeaways.title: Margins hit a record
takeaways.text: Gross margin reached 46.9% of revenue, and EPS rose 10% to an all-time record $2.40 — the mix keeps shifting toward Services, which keeps far more of each dollar than hardware.

takeaways.title: iPhone took a small step back
takeaways.text: iPhone sales slipped 1% to $69.1B and Greater China revenue fell 11%, even as Mac (+16%) and iPad (+15%) more than covered the gap.
